blogs.title: 1.58 Bits Explained: Why Ternary Weights Let LLMs Skip Multiplication
blogs.description: A friendly walkthrough of what 1.58 bits means (log2 of 3 states), how ternary weights {-1, 0, 1} work, why zero matters for feature filtering, and how BitNet b1.58 replaces costly multiplies with fast integer additions while keeping accuracy.

blogs.title: Implementing BitLinear: A hands-on guide to 1.58-bit Transformers
blogs.description: Step-by-step implementation of a BitLinear layer with the absmean quantizer, 8-bit activations, and per-token scaling. Covers training tips, stabilization tricks, and integration into popular stacks like Hugging Face, vLLM, and llama.cpp.

blogs.title: Benchmarking ternary vs FP16: Latency, memory, and energy on real hardware
blogs.description: A practical benchmarking guide comparing BitNet b1.58 to FP16 baselines across GPUs and CPUs. Shows how to measure time per token, memory footprint, throughput, and estimated energy, and what to expect as model size scales.

blogs.title: The new scaling law: Planning model size and cost with 1.58-bit LLMs
blogs.description: Explains the cost-performance equivalences (e.g., 70B 1.58-bit vs 13B FP16 cost) and how this changes capacity planning, cloud bills, and product strategy. Includes guidance on when 1.58-bit reaches parity (around 3B+) and how to pick a model size.

blogs.title: Beyond post-training quantization: Why training low-bit from scratch wins
blogs.description: Compares post-training quantization to training-with-quantization for 1.58-bit models. Discusses accuracy, stability, and why explicit zeros improve modeling, with recipes and pitfalls for practitioners moving past PTQ.

blogs.title: Long context for less: Shrinking KV caches with 1.58-bit LLMs
blogs.description: Shows how 8-bit activations and sub-8-bit strategies can cut KV cache memory, enabling longer context windows without extra hardware. Covers accuracy trade-offs, compression schemes, and throughput tuning.

blogs.title: MoE meets 1-bit: Designing sparse ternary LLMs with minimal cross-chip traffic
blogs.description: Explores how 1.58-bit weights reduce memory and interconnect bottlenecks in Mixture-of-Experts models. Presents routing considerations, deployment topologies, and how ternary MoE can fit on fewer devices.

blogs.title: Ternary LLMs on the edge: Running chatbots on laptops, phones, and microservers
blogs.description: A deployment playbook for edge and mobile: CPU-only inference, memory budgeting, thermal and battery implications, and real-world use cases unlocked by 1.58-bit models’ low footprint and energy draw.

blogs.title: Inside the energy math: Why INT8 adds beat FP16 multiplies
blogs.description: Demystifies compute energy models that show large savings from integer additions over floating-point multiplies. Connects the math to observed speedups and how power limits gate performance on modern chips.

blogs.title: Hardware wishlist: What an accelerator for 1-bit LLMs should support
blogs.description: Sketches a hardware and systems blueprint optimized for ternary models: memory hierarchy, on-chip SRAM needs, add-centric compute arrays, encoding layouts, and software kernels that exploit 1.58-bit arithmetic.
